question.problem: Find the real solution to the equation $4\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=-3.$
question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{sinh}⁡x$ is

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}).
$$

Substituting the above definition into the equation $4\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=-3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot (\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})) & =-3 \\ 2({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & =-3 \\ 2{e}^{x}-2{e}^{-x} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply both sides of the equation by ${e}^{x},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\cdot (2{e}^{x}-2{e}^{-x}) & ={e}^{x}\cdot (-3) \\ 2{e}^{2x}-2 & =-3{e}^{x} \\ 2{e}^{2x}+3{e}^{x}-2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This is a quadratic equation in ${e}^{x}$ that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2{e}^{x}-1)({e}^{x}+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

By the zero-product property, we have to solve two equations:

$$
2{e}^{x}-1=0,\,{e}^{x}+2=0
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{e}^{x}-1 & =0 &  & \, & {e}^{x}+2 & =0 \\ {e}^{x} & =\frac{1}{2} &  & \, & {e}^{x} & =-2 \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) &  & \, & \end{aligned}
$$

There are no real values of $x$ for which ${e}^{x}=-2.$ Therefore, $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2})$ is the only real solution to the equation.
